chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Khas'ami, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Abu Zarr came to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), and with him was Gabriel (peace be upon him) in the form of Dihya al-Kalbi, and the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) had secluded him (Gabriel). So when he (Abu Zarr) saw them, he turned away from them and did not cut off their conversation. So Gabriel (peace be upon him) said: 'O Muhammad! This is Abu Zarr who has passed by us and did not greet us. Had he greeted, we would have returned the greeting to him. O Muhammad! Indeed, he has a supplication which he supplicates with that is well-known among the people of the sky, so ask him about it when I ascend to the sky.'

So when Gabriel ascended, Abu Zarr came to the Prophet. So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to him: 'What prevented you, O Abu Zarr, from greeting us when you passed by us?' He said: 'I thought, O Messenger of Allah, that the one who was with you, Dihya al-Kalbi, you had secluded for one of your matters.' He (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'That was Gabriel (peace be upon him), O Abu Zarr, and he said: Had he greeted us, we would have returned the greeting to him.'

So when Abu Zarr knew that it was Gabriel (peace be upon him), regret entered him because he did not greet him, as Allah willed. So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to him: 'What is this supplication that you supplicate with, for Gabriel (peace be upon him) has informed me that you have a supplication that you supplicate with which is well-known in the sky?'

He said: 'Yes, O Messenger of Allah, I say: O Allah! I ask You for safety and faith in You, and confirmation in Your Prophet, and well-being from all affliction, and gratitude for well-being, and neediness from the evil of people.'

key_terms.اسْتَخْلَاهُ: He secluded him / kept him apart
key_terms.دِحْيَةَ الْكَلْبِيُّ: Dihya al-Kalbi, a companion often used as a disguise for Gabriel

ai.seo_question: What is the specific supplication of Abu Zarr that is well-known in the heavens?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) reveals that Abu Zarr al-Ghifari’s modesty in withholding his greeting—mistaking Gabriel for Dihya al-Kalbi—was actually a sign of deep reverence, prompting Gabriel to highlight his unique, heaven-approved supplication. This specific dua, emphasizing security, faith, and gratitude, is presented as a comprehensive spiritual remedy, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the intercessory value of the righteous and the efficacy of concise, profound supplications in navigating worldly and otherworldly needs.
